title: Start: the NEAT brief, deadline Friday 17:00
text: BRIEF.md in this folder was a stale copy of the lunarlander-98 brief, a project already finished (PPO 98.8% / 98.4%). The user confirmed the real brief is NEXT_PROJECT_BRIEF.md: NEAT from a clean start, a curriculum, a network sized by measurement, a fast C++ simulator for training, and boulder layout v3. Deadline Friday 2026-11-06 17:00, wrap-up from 16:27. Machine: i5-8250U, 4 cores / 8 threads, 7.6 GB, no usable GPU.

title: Boulder layout v3 in the frozen task
text: One approved change to the world: the boulder's bottom now stays at least 3.5 m above the pad (v2: 1.73 m, less than the lander's 1.8 m height). Same random stream as v2, so each seed keeps its boulder size and sideways position; only the height moved, into a 3.0 m band. Test: on 100,000 seeds of each of the 6 seed ranges, every clearance holds. The passability test (a planner that may read the true wind, used only as a test) comes next.

title: How big must the network be? Copies say: more than 16 hidden nodes
text: The PPO champion (16->128->128->4) was copied by imitation (DAgger, the same budget each) into small networks and each copy flew the same 1,000 fresh analysis flights of layout v3. 16->8->4: 56.5%. 16->16->4: 79.1%. 16->32->4: 87.0%. The PPO original: 98.9% (its first number on v3; failures: 10 boulder touches, 1 crash). So small networks are not enough. The copies are only a yardstick: NEAT starts from random genomes. The test was stopped before the bigger sizes when the user asked to go straight to NEAT.

title: Run N1 starts: NEAT from random genomes, goal 95%
text: The user's decision today: NEAT from scratch with a curriculum, a population big enough to evolve, nodes that can be added and removed; stop at 95% or Friday 17:00 (the brief's 98% is lowered to 95%). Set-up: population 300, every genome 16 inputs -> 32 random tanh hidden nodes -> 4 outputs (640 connections), weights random; mutation nudges 80% of weights by N(0, 0.1), adds nodes (3%) and connections (5%), deletes nodes (2%) and connections (2%). Speciation retuned every generation to keep ~12 species. All genomes of a generation fly the same seeds; the top 10 re-fly 40 selection seeds. Curriculum N1: calm landing with fading training wheels -> wind ramp 5->15 with turbulence -> boulder growing 0.4->1.0 with 40% real-task rehearsal -> real task with 30% hard cases. Speed in the Python reference simulator: ~40,000-50,000 steps/s on 7 workers, ~20 s per calm generation; the C++ simulator is postponed until speed is the bottleneck. Expectation written before the result: >= 90% calm landings within ~250 generations.

title: Bug found: the species threshold ran away (0.25 -> 35)
text: Check-in at gen 54. Calm landing is learned: the champion lands 100% of its calm training flights since gen 18 (training wheels still 0.82 -> 0.46), mean fitness -342 -> +179. But my speciation controller is broken: it raises the compatibility threshold 10% per generation whenever there are more than 12 species, and the count has been stuck at 14 since gen 3 while the threshold went 0.25 -> 35. neat-python keeps old species as long as genomes stay within the threshold of their representative, so the count never responded. With a threshold of 35 no new species can form; as stagnant species are removed, the population would collapse into one species and new structure would lose its protection. Change (one): clamp the threshold to 0.15-1.0 and step it 5% per generation; reset it to 0.5 at the restart. Expectation before the result: the species count should drift towards ~12, and calm-landing progress should not suffer.

title: Stage 1 passed; species down to 3, so the threshold floor goes 0.15 -> 0.05
text: Stage 1 (calm landing) passed at gen 100: the champion landed 96.5% of 200 fresh calm flights with no training wheels, confirmed at 97.5% on another fresh 200. Stage 2 (wind ramp) started; at gen 151 the push is 7.5 (75% steady) and the champion still lands all its training flights; the real task is at 6% (best so far). Problem: species fell from 13 to 3 (exactly 100 genomes each) with the threshold stuck at its floor 0.15. Measured on the gen-150 checkpoint: genomes are a median 0.94 apart, but each species is one tight lineage whose members are within 0.15 of each other, so no new species can split off while stagnation removes old ones down to the 3 protected by species_elitism. Change (one): lower the threshold floor to 0.05 so the controller can split lineages again (target ~12). Expectation before the result: species back to 8-12 within ~30 generations, no drop in the champion's landing rate.

title: The champion's network is now saved at every check
text: For The model tab (the user asked to see the network and how it develops): the trainer now saves the generation champion's network every 10 generations (runs/N1/champions/*_track.json). No change to evolution itself. Restarted from the checkpoint.

title: Correction: species collapsed because of a resume bug, not the threshold floor
text: At the 16:45 check-in I blamed the species collapse (13 -> 3) on the threshold floor of 0.15 and lowered it to 0.05. That was wrong: species stayed at 3. Measured on the gen-195 checkpoint: members sit 0.37-0.48 from their representative, which is impossible with a threshold of 0.05. Cause: when the run resumes, the species set comes back from the pickle with its own copy of the settings, so speciation kept the threshold it had at the first restart (gen 57): 46.8, the runaway value. Since gen 57 every genome was lumped into an existing species and stagnation removed them down to the 3 protected by species_elitism; my controller was tuning a number nobody read. Fix: on resume, the species set and the trainer share one settings object, and a test checks it. Expectation before the result: new species form within a few generations (threshold restarts at 0.3), heading for ~12.

title: Crash after the species fix; threshold set by measurement
text: After the resume fix, the threshold I restarted with (0.3) split the population into 105 species, and neat-python stopped with an error (105 species x 3 genomes minimum > 300 genomes). The supervisor restarted it twice from the gen-196 checkpoint with the same result; no generations were lost beyond these retries. This time I chose the threshold by simulation on the saved population: 0.3 -> 79 species, 0.4 -> 13, 0.45 -> 6, 0.5 and above -> 3. Set to 0.4. Guard added so this cannot stop the run again: when there are very many species, the per-species minimum and elitism shrink for that generation and the threshold rises 30% per generation instead of 5%.

title: Wind ramp review: paced ramps, early pass, boulder practice, automatic end
text: Diagnosis (200 analysis flights each): the gen-211 champion landed 97.5% in its current training world, 67% in full wind without a boulder (gen 100: 15.5%), 0% in calm air with a boulder (73% boulder hits), 1% on the real task. So wind learning works; the low real-task line is the boulder, which the curriculum had not trained yet, and the fixed-clock ramp was slow while the champion landed 97-100% of its flights. Changes at gen 230: (1) ramps are paced: 3 steps per generation while the champion lands >= 90% of its own flights in the current world, 1 at >= 70%, 0.5 below; (2) the stage's final world is checked every 10 generations from the start and passing it (plus confirmation) ends the stage at once, even mid-ramp; (3) 25% of stage-2 flights carry a 40%-size boulder (not counted for pace or pass) so route learning starts early; (4) at the deadline (minus 20 min) the trainer stops, re-flies the 5 best-checked champions plus the newest on 1,000 fresh selection flights and picks one; the supervisor then flies both test blocks automatically, also after a goal stop; (5) the local dashboard shows the newest champion flying in its current world. First check after the change: real task 15.5% (new best), stage final world 61%.

title: Training 5x faster: C++ simulator for training flights
text: From gen 267 the training flights of N1 run in C++ (sim/lander_sim.cpp: the same Box2D 2.3.x that box2d-py wraps, plus the NEAT network). Gens 236-251 took 95 s each (32,500 steps/s), gens 252-266 with the fast Python path and a numba network 48 s, and now 18 s (~166,000 steps/s), so ~195 generations an hour instead of 38. Equivalence test on 1,000 analysis seeds in three worlds: bit-identical to a fresh reference env on 3,000 of 3,000 flights, and the same outcome as the reused reference env on 99.7-100% (as often as the reference agrees with itself). Checks, the selection and the goal test still fly the reference Python env; lander/env.py is unchanged. Details on the Speed tab.

title: NEAT itself 4.6x faster between generations
text: After the C++ switch the flights took 18 s per generation but the wall clock 27 s: neat-python spent ~6 s per generation on crossover (its feed-forward cycle check rescans every connection for every inherited gene) and speciation distances while all workers waited. RandomStartGenome now overrides both with the same logic, the same random draws and the same sums: identical populations and species over 3 generations from the N1 checkpoint. From gen 313: ~19 s per generation wall clock (~101 s before today's speed work), ~190 generations an hour. Correction: the earlier note's '~195 an hour' counted flying time only; the wall-clock rate then was ~134.

title: Worker count measured: 8
text: Same 7 generations from the gen-326 checkpoint with 4-8 workers: 22.8, 21.4, 20.2, 19.3 and 18.9 s per generation (7 and 8 alternated three times; 8 won every pair, by ~2%). Going from 4 to 8 workers gains only 17%: 4 physical cores, and hyperthreads add little. N1 continues from gen 327 with 8 workers. The top 10's re-flights now fly the exact fast Python env (the reference's numbers step for step); checks and the champion's selection flights stay in the reference env.

title: Where the champion fails: the wind, not the boulder
text: The user asked whether to restart the curriculum with a small boulder and no wind, then light wind, ramping both. Measured first (experiments/wind_boulder_grid.py, gen-382 champion, 400 analysis flights per cell, C++ sim): calm air lands 86% / 90% (no / full boulder), wind 5: 96% / 85%, wind 10: 94% / 75%, full wind 15 + turbulence 1.5: 73% / 53%. The boulder is already handled in calm and light wind; the bottleneck is strong gusty wind (crashes 15-16%, off-pad 7-9%). So no restart. Proposed instead (waiting for the user): stage 3 ramps wind 10 -> 15 together with the boulder, with ~30% real-task rehearsal. N1 continues unchanged meanwhile.

title: Stage 3 ended at its cap (gen 702) without a pass; stage 4 (real task + hard cases) started
text: The boulder reached full size at gen 578 (paced ramp, mostly at half speed since the champion landed ~60-75% of its flights). Stage 3 needed 85% on the real task and ended at its 400-generation cap instead. Real-task checks (200 fresh flights every 10 gens) averaged 59% over stage 3 and 65% over gens 640-692; the best single check is still 76% at gen 402 (likely partly luck: 200 flights). Stage 4 now flies the real task, with 30% of flights re-flying seeds recent champions failed (hard cases). Still at ~19.5 s per generation. Open question for the user (wind 10->15 together with the boulder) is moot now that stage 3 is over; the hard-case stage is the next lever.
